answer: Anchor each agent's identity to a verifiable work history: an agent must complete small paid tasks over time before it can transact at scale, so a new identity starts with a hollow reputation. Sybil attackers then face a real cost — every fake identity must earn trust slowly, and an onyx-blacklist of proven bad actors makes abandoned identities worthless to reuse. A flood of fresh identities cannot fake the time and work that trust requires.
